title: Space bound for compiled computation
statement: Let the program state set and decider state set be finite. Let $P$ be a register program with $m$ registers and $d$ oracle deciders, and let $D$ be a decider machine with $k_D$ work tapes. Choose a start state, initial decider states, an oracle, register-head bounds $lo,hi$, and natural numbers $B,N$; let $w$ be a bit word. Suppose the register-program run on $x$ is halted at time $N$ with output $w$, its register heads stay between $lo$ and $hi$ through time $N$, and at every earlier time its calls satisfy the conditions that argument registers are distinct, the input head is at position $1$, each argument register stores its represented word from cell $0$ with head at $0$ and word length within the bounds, and the corresponding decider run halts with the oracle's answer, clears its work tapes, returns their heads to $0$, and keeps each decider head within distance $B$ of $0$. Then the compiled finite machine halts on $x$ with output $w$ after some time $T$, and its total space use is at most $\sum_r (hi(r)-lo(r)+1) + k_D(2B+1)$.
